terms.definition: The largest value in quantity or degree in a set of values.
A mean of a set of observations where the mathematic calculation is unspecified or unknown.

The n-th root of the multiple products of n values; a geometric average.
The middle value in an ordered set of values. In the case of an even number of values, it is the average of the two middle values.
The smallest value in quantity or degree in a set of values.
The lowest value in terms of position, place, magnitude, level, or rank.
A textual description of the particulars of an act, occurrence, or course of events.
A scale or classification with no inherent order to the values, which uses named categories or labels.
A scale that uses an ordered set of values where the difference between successive designations may not be constant.
A numeric measure of a physical attribute of an entity or substance.
An estimated numeric measure of an entity or substance whose values could be a range, non-linear, or non-continuous.
The outward or visible aspect of an entity.
The quantity of a specified substance, which is subject to individual judgment, preference, or predetermined reference, in a unit volume or weight of another substance.
The extent of a 2-dimensional surface enclosed within a boundary. (NCI)
The volume consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per area per unit of time.
The quantity of a specified substance, which is based on catalytic activity, in a unit volume or weight of another substance.
The total amount of catalytic activity for a substance contained within an entity.
The catalytic activity of a component substance to the catalytic activity of the whole represented as a decimal between 0 and 1.
The catalytic activity of a component substance to the catalytic activity of the whole.
The enzymatic activity of a specified component divided by the number of molar entities.
The weight of a specified component divided by the number of entities.
The molar amount of a specified component divided by the number of entities.
The volume of a specified component divided by the number of entities.
The degree or magnitude of fluorescent light emission.
A diagnostic statement that is an interpretation or abstraction of an observation(s).

The weight of a component substance to the weight of the whole.
The weight consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per unit of time.
The quotient of the weight of one substance divided by the weight of another substance.
The amount of matter in an object.
A statement about the form and/or structure of a target entity.
The individual test result relative to the median value of a reference set of test results.
The number of specified entities per unit of area.
The number of specified entities in a unit volume or weight of a substance.
The number of component entities to the total number of entities.

The difference between two numbers divided by the average of the two numbers, multiplied by 100.
Any of the 99 intermediate points that divide an ordered set of scores into 100 parts, each of which contains one-hundredth of the total.
An indication of the presence of an entity which, if present, is identified.
An indication of the presence of an entity which, if present, is in an amount above a predetermined threshold.
Any of the 4 intermediate points that divide an ordered set of scores into 5 parts, each of which contains one-twentieth of the total.
The relationship in quantity, amount, or size between two entities or activities.

The density of a specified substance, relative to a comparator.
The quantity, expressed as a weight, of a specified substance in a unit volume or weight of another substance, relative to a comparator.
The time of a specified activity, relative to a comparator.
The degree or extent to which something is dissolved, absorbed, or bound compared with the maximum physical limit under defined conditions.
A value (e.g., number, numeric range, ratio) that assesses and orders a result or response for purposes of comparison.
The quantity, expressed in moles, of a specified substance in a unit volume or weight of another substance.
The molar amount of a component substance to the molar amount of the whole.
The molar amount of substance consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per unit of time.
The quotient of the molar amount of one substance, divided by the molar amount of another substance.
The number or limit on a scale that defines when a threshold, or cut-off, is reached.
The quotient of one activity time interval divided by another activity time interval.
The length of time during which something continues.
Concentration of a substance in a solution as determined by the quantitative reaction with added measured volume(s) of a solution of the precisely known concentration(s) of a standard reagent.
An identifiable class based on common distinguishable qualities.
The speed of an entity in a given direction.
The resistance of a liquid to sheer forces and flow. (NCI)
Quotient of the volume of a component substance to the sum of the volumes of all component substances represented as a decimal between 0 and 1.
Quotient of the volume of a component substance to the sum of the volumes of all component substances.
The volume consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per unit of time.
The amount of three dimensional space occupied by an object or the capacity of a space or container. (NCI)
The number of positive or negative standard deviations of a measured value from the mean of its population.

An assay type that examines the interaction of ligands with their target biomolecules.
